name: Tight braids, weaves and extensions on relaxed hair
what_people_do: Put in tight cornrows, braids or extensions as a protective, low-maintenance style for weeks at a time.
why_they_say_it_works: Protects the ends, saves daily styling and keeps hair "tucked away".

documented_by.source: Hairdressing and scalp disease in African adults (Cape Town, n=874), 2007, Br J Dermatol, PMID 17725667
documented_by.quote_or_summary: Cape Town adults, 874: women's traction alopecia was 31.7% and was 48% when the usual style was extensions attached to relaxed hair.

documented_by.source: Hairdressing and scalp disease in African schoolchildren (n=1042), 2007, Br J Dermatol, PMID 17553035
documented_by.quote_or_summary: Cape Town schoolchildren: traction alopecia 9.4% overall, 17.1% in girls, higher with relaxed than natural hair.

documented_by.source: Hair grooming practices of women of African descent in London, 2016, J Eur Acad Dermatol Venereol, PMID 27038251
documented_by.quote_or_summary: London: hair was washed on average every 17.9 days, rising to 32.8 days when braided or in a weave; only 46.3% avoided braiding relaxed hair.

evidence.finding: Highest risk when traction added to relaxed hair (OR 3.47); only 18.9% of women with TA had never noticed hairdressing symptoms.

source.name: Determinants of marginal traction alopecia in African girls and women, 2008, J Am Acad Dermatol, PMID 18694677

evidence.finding: High-, moderate- and low-risk styles; limited literature.

source.name: Haskin A, Aguh C 2016, J Am Acad Dermatol, PMID 27114262

harm_note: Traction alopecia can become permanent scarring hair loss; tightness and hairline pain are the early signs.
gaps: Cross-sectional, no trial of loosening styles.
